sections.title: Market Pulse: First Winning Week in Three

items.headline: U.S. Stocks Close Higher, Marking First Winning Week in Three
items.summary: U.S. equity markets ended Friday's session broadly higher, securing their first weekly gain in three weeks. The positive momentum was driven by a notable cooldown in oil prices and an easing of Treasury yields, providing Wall Street with crucial breathing room after a turbulent week that included a Federal Reserve rate hike and a U.S.-China summit.

items.headline: Moderna Leads Weekly Gains on Strong Performance
items.summary: Moderna ($MRNA) was a top performer for the week, surging 29.08% to close at $198.88. (Note: Weekly performance, daily details not available).

items.headline: Datadog Shows Robust Weekly Growth
items.summary: Datadog ($DDOG) experienced significant weekly growth, up 16.61% to $268.02. (Note: Weekly performance, daily details not available).

items.headline: Dell Rises Amid Information Technology Sector Strength
items.summary: Dell ($DELL) was a top performer in the Information Technology sector, which led all sectors on Friday. This was supported by Morgan Stanley raising its bull-case price target for the company to $756.

items.headline: Tesla Shares Dip on Analyst Downgrades
items.summary: Tesla ($TSLA) shares closed down 1.54% at $372.11 on Friday, as analyst cuts overshadowed the company's plans to ramp Semi Truck production.

items.headline: Gen Digital Experiences Sharp Weekly Decline
items.summary: Gen Digital ($GEN) was among the worst-performing stocks of the week, falling 25.47% to end at $21.62. (Note: Weekly performance, daily details not available).

items.headline: Devon Energy and Sector Hit by Falling Oil Prices
items.summary: Devon Energy ($DVN) and other energy stocks traded lower on Friday as Brent crude oil prices fell 2% to $104 per barrel, impacting revenue expectations.

items.headline: Technology and Healthcare Lead, Energy and Utilities Lag
items.summary: For the week ending September 25, Technology was the best-performing sector, rising 3.1%, followed by Healthcare, up 1.57%. Information Technology also led all sectors on Friday with a 0.99% gain, driven by semiconductor and AI-related stocks. Conversely, Energy and Utilities were the worst performers for the week, declining 3.07% and 3.04% respectively. On Friday, the Energy sector lagged with a 0.88% loss, while Materials fell 1.2%.

items.headline: Strong Economic Data Fuels Rate Hike Expectations
items.summary: Recent economic data indicated a robust economy. S&P Global's flash composite PMI for September surged to 58.4, its highest in over five years, signaling accelerating growth in manufacturing and services. Initial jobless claims also fell to 197,000, near multi-decade lows. These strong prints pushed market expectations for an October Fed rate hike to roughly 70%. U.S. new home sales jumped 6.4% in August, reaching the highest level since December 2025.

items.headline: Oil Prices Cool, Treasury Yields Ease From Highs
items.summary: A cooldown in Brent crude oil prices, which dropped below $98 a barrel and fell 2.46% to $92.28/barrel on Friday, helped alleviate pressure on Wall Street. This also contributed to Treasury yields easing after the 10-year yield briefly touched its highest level since 2007. The 10-year Treasury yield closed the week up about 15 basis points to 5.15%, having topped 5.20% earlier in the week.

items.headline: Q3 Earnings Season Approaching with Strong Growth Expectations
items.summary: The third-quarter earnings season is on the horizon, with S&P 500 earnings anticipated to grow by 23.9% year-over-year. This marks the eighth consecutive quarter of double-digit earnings growth for the index, driven significantly by the Technology sector. Oracle and Adobe reported their fiscal quarters ending in August, which contribute to the Q3 tally.

items.headline: U.S.-China Summit Concludes, Iran Diplomacy Continues
items.summary: A summit between Presidents Trump and Xi Jinping concluded, with discussions encompassing AI, the Iran conflict, and tariffs. The two leaders agreed to extend their trade truce by two months. Meanwhile, hopes for a swift diplomatic resolution with Iran waned after Iran's president's speech at the UN General Assembly, although discussions regarding reopening the Strait of Hormuz did contribute to lower oil prices.
